board.about: The Reviews board's tools, run by the agent socket's `reviews` command (`tool`, `params`); `help` lists them. writes: they change the user's lists.

tools.name: effort_get
tools.description: An upstreaming effort: its declaration (source, target, feeders, head workspace), counts by disposition (upstream, in_review, in_part, planned, not_for_upstream, superseded, unsorted), feeders with commits not on the source yet, overlaps with other efforts and branches, and the last bulk changes.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

tools.name: effort_set
tools.description: Declare an upstreaming effort on a group or a workspace headed upstream (group, source branch; target defaults to origin/main, the clone to the group's first workspace), or change one (effort). preview: true only says what it would hold and its overlaps. Declaring never starts a session. The user is told and can undo it.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

group.description: To declare one: the group headed upstream (path, name or id), or a workspace headed upstream by itself (name or checkout path).

source.description: The branch followed: a ref name, resolved once to one exact ref of the clone (the local branch first; refused when only several remote ones fit).

head.description: The head workspace: its name or checkout path.

preview.description: Only say what it would hold and its overlaps; save nothing.

tools.name: effort_delete
tools.description: Delete an upstreaming effort (by id, or by name when no other effort has it): only when the user asked. Its declaration leaves Reviews with its card, ledger marks, plans and history; the other efforts' ledgers, its parts' branches and worktrees are never touched. The user sees it with Undo, which brings it all back.

effort.description: The effort: its id (effort_get), or its name when no other effort has it.

tools.name: ledger_list
tools.description: An effort's commits, oldest first, 200 a page (cursor), each with sha, subject, author, top directory, disposition and note; filter with words and disposition:, dir:, file:, author: tokens. cluster: true adds a first grouping of the unsorted commits for proposing planned requests.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

filter.description: Words (subject, sha) and disposition:, dir:, file:, author: tokens.

cluster.description: Also a first grouping of the unsorted commits (fixups with their commit, by directory and subject prefix), smallest first: material for planned requests.

tools.name: ledger_set
tools.description: Set the disposition of up to 500 commits of an effort at once (not_for_upstream with a reason, superseded with a pointer, planned, upstream or in_review by hand, unsorted to clear), all or nothing. The user sees it with Undo.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

commits.description: Shas (7 characters at least) or ledger keys.

pointer.description: superseded: what replaces it; upstream / in_review by hand: the commit or request.

tools.name: effort_overlaps
tools.description: The other efforts and branches headed upstream holding commits of this effort (same, contains, contained, partial) and the proposed layout for each; nothing is applied.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

tools.name: ledger_match
tools.description: Confirm (accept: true) or reject fuzzy matches of an effort's commits: upstream commits Roamgate proposes as the same change under another patch id (ledger_list shows them as proposals). A confirmed one makes the commit upstream by hand, pointing at that upstream commit; a rejected one is never proposed again. All or nothing; the user sees it with Undo.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

tools.name: ledger_plans
tools.description: The effort's planned requests (each the content of one future request): propose one (plan: its name, commits, depends_on), accept, edit (name, commits, add, remove, depends_on), split (commits moved to a new plan called name) or drop one. A commit is in one planned request only, across efforts. As the effort's leader you propose; the user accepts (accept only when they said so). The user sees it with Undo.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

plan.description: The planned request (name or id); propose: its name.

name.description: edit: a new name; split: the new plan's name.

commits.description: propose: its commits; edit: all of them; split: those moved to the new plan.

tools.name: part_create
tools.description: Make the part of an accepted planned request: a worktree workspace (through the user's worktree command) placed under the effort's head workspace in the Workspaces tree, or in the effort's group when it has no head, on its base, with the plan's commits cherry-picked in source order (messages kept as written), then every fixup!, squash! and amend! commit folded into its target in the part (a squash! adds its body to the target's message; folded counts them); a fixup whose target is not in the part stays a commit and is reported in unfolded. Its base (base says which) is the branch of the part of the plan it depends_on (the last one in source order when several have parts), or, for a plan made only of fixups of another plan's commits, that plan's part (refused, naming it, while that plan has no part); the target otherwise. When a local branch upstream/<plan name> (or the branch named by from) already holds the plan's changes over the target, the part starts at its commit instead and nothing is picked (from says which). When that branch is a port of the plan (its content differs: voice stripped, retitled, reworked) and sits on the part's base (it contains the base, or is built on the target or on the upstream branch of the part it depends on, none of its commits the source's), the part starts there as well: ported: true, and differs lists the files only in the plan and only in the branch; the source's commits are then never picked. That branch is only read, never moved. Always a new branch at a path that did not exist (an existing branch is refused; a taken path gets a -part suffix); picked counts only the commits read back on the branch, folding checked to keep its tree. A conflict stops the pick (or the folding) and is reported (commit and files); nothing is aborted: resolve it in that worktree. Its branch is then a request not proposed yet. With refresh: true, for a plan that has its part (moved by hand onto a port or a squashed commit, say), nothing is made, picked or moved: its worktree (the path recorded) and the branch it is on now are only read, and the part's record is rewritten (journaled, the user can undo it): base (the depends_on part whose tip its branch holds, else the target), from (the branch from names, else an upstream/* branch at its commit), ported and differs (it does not hold the plan's changes as they are but is a port of them on its base), picked (plan changes present), folded and unfolded (the fixups its branch still holds as commits) and conflict (a stop in its worktree). A worktree or branch gone is refused, saying so; then from names an existing local branch to attach the part to: its worktree when it has one, else a new worktree at a free path on it (that branch not moved). Never pushes or opens anything on a forge.

effort.description: The effort: its name or id.

branch.description: The part's branch; the plan's name otherwise.

from.description: A local branch to start the part at, nothing picked (upstream/<plan name> is tried by itself): one holding the plan's changes over the target, or a port of the plan sitting on the part's base and touching its files; refused otherwise. With refresh: the branch recorded as the part's from, or, when its worktree or branch is gone, the existing local branch to attach the part to.

refresh.description: Refresh the plan's existing part: read its record again from its branch as it is now; nothing made or moved.

tools.name: upstream_group
tools.description: Mark a Workspaces-tree group as headed upstream (its workspaces, and those of the groups inside it, hold work meant to go upstream: their branches show in Reviews, lane Not proposed upstream yet, until their request opens), or unmark it. Only when the user asked.

group.description: A Workspaces-tree group: its path of names ("Upstream/Media"), its name when only one group has it, or its id.

tools.name: upstream_workspace
tools.description: Say one workspace of a group headed upstream is not (headed: false), or is again; a workspace in no such group is headed upstream by itself (headed: true) or no longer. Only when the user asked.

workspace.description: A workspace: its name or its checkout path (in the Workspaces tree or not).

headed.description: false: not headed upstream (skipped in its group, unmarked alone); true: headed upstream (back in its group, marked alone).

tools.name: upstream_unsent
tools.description: Turn a branch headed upstream into a request not proposed yet (with a title and target branch, the first commit's subject and the default branch otherwise), or back into a plain branch. When its request opens on the forge it takes the request's place, order and what was set by hand. Never opens anything on a forge.

branch.description: A branch headed upstream: its key from reviews_list, or its branch name when only one has it.

unsent.description: true: it will be a request (not proposed yet); false: a plain branch again.

tools.name: reviews_view
tools.description: Create (or change the query of) a saved view of the user's Reviews list, a chip after All / To review / Mine on every device, or delete one. The query is reviews_list's filter (tokens and words). Only when the user asked for it.

filter.description: The view's query, as reviews_list's filter.

tools.name: reviews_list
tools.description: The inbox exactly as the user sees it, in their order: for each request its position (# overall, n in its section), section (pinned, for_you: to review, authored: their own, suggested), key, reference, title, author, state, pipeline, updated, what is new (unread: new commits and comments, or new when never opened), the suggestion's score and reason, the pinned flag, and for the user's own requests their lane (needs you (your_move), waiting, merging, blocked, not_sent, stale, done), why, the next step, a merge scheduled by a label or a bot merging it (merge: after {label, delay, from, mergeable_at, ready}, bot {name, via, queued, position, failed {reason, at}}) and where it comes from, what was set by hand (override, maybe outdated) and the requests each waits for (under: drawn below that one); plus the removed (hidden) requests. Paged: limit (at most 120) and cursor (next_cursor of the last page). Use it before reordering, and to answer "what is on my list". No forge call.

text.description: Keep requests with any of these words (case-insensitive) in their reference, title, project or author.

filter.description: The panel's search: key:value tokens (project:group/name or group/*, label:x, waiting:me|reviewer|external|NAME, lane:needs-you|waiting|merging|blocked|not-sent|stale|done, state:open|draft|merging|merged|closed|branch|unsent, merge-after:yes|no|waiting|ready, bot:NAME|any|queued|failed, waiting:time|BOT, stale:yes, draft:yes|no, author:NAME, pipeline:failed|running|success|manual, effort:NAME, is:mine|review|pinned|suggested|unread; any negated with -; several of one key: any) and words; or view:NAME for a saved view.

tools.name: reviews_order
tools.description: Reorder the user's list. The order is the user's own and shared live by all their devices (desktop, phone, app), so move only what they asked and leave the rest. Moves apply to the latest order, so a change the user just made is kept. place top / bottom puts the requests at the top / bottom of their own section (Pinned, For you, Suggested are separate lists: to put one above all of them, pin it with reviews_pin); before / after place them beside target (in its section); exact puts the listed ones first, in the order given. keys and target are keys from a tool result, references (project!123, owner/repo#123) or URLs of requests in the list. Returns what moved, keys not in the list (unknown) and keys in another section than the target (elsewhere), and the new top of each section changed. The user is told and can undo it. Only when the user asked for an order.

items.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

keys.description: The requests to move, in the order they should end up in.

place.description: top / bottom of their section; before / after the request named in target; exact: these first, in this order (the others follow unchanged).

target.description: The request place before / after refers to.

tools.name: reviews_pin
tools.description: Add a request to the user's view by URL or reference (it stays listed in Pinned, as the panel's p does), even if no query finds it. Only when the user asked.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

tools.name: reviews_unpin
tools.description: Take a request out of Pinned (the panel's dd on a pinned request). Only when the user asked.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

tools.name: reviews_hide
tools.description: Remove a request from the user's view until something happens on it (a push, a comment, a state change), as dd does in the panel; a pinned request is unpinned instead. It is listed with the hidden ones. Only when the user asked.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

tools.name: reviews_unhide
tools.description: Bring a removed (hidden) request back into the view, as H and restore do in the panel. Only when the user asked.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

tools.name: reviews_sort
tools.description: Set the user's order once from a sort, in one section or all (score: the suggestion score, highest first; updated: most recent first; project: by project, then most recent; unread: new and changed first). It does not keep sorting: later changes and the user's own moves stand. It replaces the user's own arrangement of that section, so use it only when the user asked to sort; for "put X first" use reviews_order.

tools.name: reviews_refresh
tools.description: Read the user's inbox again from the forges now (through its own budget), or, with request, infer again whose move it is and the next step of one of their own requests or branches (Claude reads its status, threads and description; what was set by hand still wins). Returns its lane and next step.

request.description: One of the user's own requests or branches: infer whose move it is now. Without it, read the inbox again.

tools.name: reviews_override
tools.description: Set or clear, by hand, what Roamgate says of one of the user's own requests: whose move it is (me, reviewer, external or a person), the next step, the requests it waits for (drawn under them, counted Blocked), labels, a link (URL or path) and stale. Each field set wins over what Roamgate infers; whose and next show as outdated once the request moves on. Use it when the user said so, or to record what you found ("waiting on bob's answer"). The user is told and can undo it. No forge call.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

whose.description: Whose move it is: me (the user), reviewer, external (CI, another project), or a person's user name.

next.description: The next step, in a few words.

items.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

depends_on.description: The requests it waits for (references, URLs or keys); replaces the list.

link.description: A URL or an absolute path (notes, a plan).

reviews-agent.about: The Reviews panel's agent: its own tools, then the board's, as one Ranger-style table.

tools.name: known_requests
tools.description: What Roamgate already knows, without a forge call: the inbox's For you requests (review requested, assigned, mentioned), its suggestions with the reason each was picked and its score, and the followed projects' other open requests (not suggested, with the curation's score when ranked). Use it first, and to explain a suggestion.

text.description: Words matched (case-insensitive, any of them) in references (12967, !12967), titles, projects, authors and changed paths. Omit to list everything.

tools.name: interest_signals
tools.description: The user's interest signals, as the suggestions use them: paths they committed to lately in their clones (with counts), their unmerged branches' paths, people they review, requests they reviewed, their own hints, and their feedback (more like this / not interested). No forge call.

tools.name: search_requests
tools.description: Search merge and pull requests on the forges (read only, counted against a small budget per question: search once with good filters rather than many times). GitLab searches titles and descriptions; GitHub its search syntax. 'path' keeps those changing a matching file. Without 'project', searches the followed projects. Default state opened, at most 30 per project.

text.description: Words searched in titles and descriptions by the forge.

path.description: Keep requests changing a path containing this (case-insensitive), e.g. 'validate/' or 'rtp'. Applied to each request's changed files.

project.description: One project (group/name or owner/repo). Omit for the followed projects.

updated_after.description: YYYY-MM-DD, or a number of days back such as 7d.

tools.name: request_files
tools.description: One request's changed files (with added and deleted lines), labels and description. One forge call unless already read.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

tools.name: suggest
tools.description: Put a request in the user's Suggested list, with a one-line reason. Only when the user asked for suggestions or to add it.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

reason.description: One line naming the concrete signal (a path, a person, a hint).

tools.name: feedback
tools.description: Record the user's word on a request, as x and + do in the inbox: not_interested hides it and steers suggestions away from similar ones, more_like_this toward them, none takes it back. Only when the user said so.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

tools.name: set_hints
tools.description: Change the user's own hints for the suggestions (areas they maintain, people they work with), in their words. Only when the user asked; returns the previous hints.

tools.name: open_review
tools.description: Show a request's review in Roamgate for the user, as Enter in the Reviews inbox does (its project's review worktree, shown in its workspace's Changes view; any question, such as which clone, is asked to the user there). Only when the user asked to open or review it.

request.description: The request: its key from a tool result, "project!123" (GitLab), "owner/repo#123" (GitHub), "!123" or "#123" when only one known request has that number, or its URL.

Moves apply to the latest order, so a change the user just made is kept. place top / bottom puts the requests at the top / bottom of their own section (Pinned, For you, Suggested are separate lists: to put one above all of them, pin it with reviews_pin); before / after place them beside target (in its section); exact puts the listed ones first, in the order given. keys and target are keys from a tool result, references (project!123, owner/repo#123) or URLs of requests in the list. Returns what moved, keys not in the list (unknown) and keys in another section than the target (elsewhere), and the new top of each section changed. The user is told and can undo it. Only when the user asked for an order.

tools.description: Remove a request from the user's view until something happens on it (a push, a comment, a state change), as dd does in the panel; a pinned request is unpinned instead. It is listed with the hidden ones. Only when the user asked.

tools.name: reviews_sort
tools.description: Set the user's order once from a sort, in one section or all (score: the suggestion score, highest first; updated: most recent first; project: by project, then most recent; unread: new and changed first). It does not keep sorting: later changes and the user's own moves stand. It replaces the user's own arrangement of that section, so use it only when the user asked to sort; for "put X first" use reviews_order.

tools.name: reviews_refresh
tools.description: Read the user's inbox again from the forges now (through its own budget), or, with request, infer again whose move it is and the next step of one of their own requests or branches (Claude reads its status, threads and description; what was set by hand still wins). Returns its lane and next step.

request.description: One of the user's own requests or branches: infer whose move it is now. Without it, read the inbox again.

tools.name: reviews_override
tools.description: Set or clear, by hand, what Roamgate says of one of the user's own requests: whose move it is (me, reviewer, external or a person), the next step, the requests it waits for (drawn under them, counted Blocked), labels, a link (URL or path) and stale. Each field set wins over what Roamgate infers; whose and next show as outdated once the request moves on. Use it when the user said so, or to record what you found ("waiting on bob's answer"). The user is told and can undo it. No forge call.

tools.name: work_list
tools.description: The Work board: work items by project (roamgate by default) with id, title, state (you: waits on the user, doing, verify, open, done), tags, owner (a session address and its subagent task), source, links (review threads, efforts, requests, commits, branches, decisions, files, other items), done_when (how it becomes done by itself), ask and answers (what the user has to do on a you or verify item) and times; filter by state, open, tags (all), owner, words, workspace (the items added from a workspace: its name, its ws:NAME tag, or self for yours). A project lists its subprojects' items too (each item says its project). item: one item with its description (and its earlier versions with versions: true) and comments (a thread on one of the comments is listed under that comment as its threads, with on.quote the words it quotes; answer it with review_reply on its own thread id). Use it before changing the board, and to answer "what is on the list". Without this tool (a session started before Roamgate's mod had it, a subagent that cannot load it), the review client does the same from the repository's directory: `roamgate-review work TOOL 'JSON'`.

tools.name: work_add
tools.description: Add a work item: a title, its project, a state (open by default; you when it waits on the user, doing when you take it), tags, an owner {session, task?} (session: yours from agent_sessions, refused when no connection knows it; task: the agent id of a subagent you spawned, taken as given; without an owner, the project's coordinator session owns it and is told of it), links (a review thread it came from, the commit its fix landed in, an RFC's decision: an item whose links are all decisions is done once every one is ticked; the plan, doc or RFC it follows, as a file link, so the user opens it in one tap). text: its description, the first comment of its thread. Importing: source names where it came from (the same source again changes that item instead of adding one: the answer says updated: true and what changed, the text is left aside, and a different title is refused unless replace: true), created_at / done_at keep its dates, adopt_thread makes an existing review thread the item's own (comments and ids kept). An item you add gets your workspace's tag (ws:NAME, the workspace's name) when your workspace belongs to the project's tree and is not its coordinator's: the board opened from that workspace shows its items; workspace: false leaves it out when the item is not about your workspace's work. Answers the item, its review, thread (its description's) and adopted_thread. The user sees it on the Work board; a For you item notifies them once. An item you put in you (For you) or verify must say what the user has to do: ask, one or two sentences ("Choose: media to the car with the phone mic, or no music on car links", "Dictate once after 10 idle minutes; text should appear"), and for a decision answers, a few short one-tap choices (each tap is the user's comment on the item, reaching its owner; the user can also reply in their own words, so no "Something else" answer); without an ask the move is refused. Leaving those states clears them unless given. Without this tool (a session started before Roamgate's mod had it, a subagent that cannot load it), the review client does the same from the repository's directory: `roamgate-review work TOOL 'JSON'`.

ranger.about: Ranger's tools when every handler is given (a turn gets those its handlers allow), in a turn that proposes.

tools.name: workspace_status
tools.description: List authorized workspaces, panes, agents and task status. A pane whose session a usage limit stopped has usage_limit: when the limit resets and when Roamgate resumes it (null: the user resumes it). Omit identifiers to list the authorized scope.

tools.name: workspace_history
tools.description: Read history from an authorized workspace. Use identifiers from workspace_status. Unavailable for workspaces that workspace_status reports with remote_platform "windows".

tools.name: workspace_diff
tools.description: Read working-tree changes from an authorized workspace. Use identifiers from workspace_status. Omit path to list changed files, then pass an entry's path and kind to read its diff. Supported kinds are staged, unstaged, untracked and conflicted; omitting kind reads unstaged changes. Unavailable for workspaces that workspace_status reports with remote_platform "windows".

tools.name: workspace_terminal
tools.description: Read recent terminal output from an authorized workspace. Use identifiers from workspace_status. Choose lines from 1 to 1000 (default 120); request more when earlier context is needed. Available output depends on Herdr support and agent state; application-owned history may remain unavailable. Results retain at most 32,000 newest characters and indicate truncation.

tools.name: propose_workspace_create
tools.description: Propose creating a workspace from an authorized source workspace. Returns a pending proposal for the user to confirm; does not create it.

tools.name: propose_worktree_create
tools.description: Propose creating a Git worktree from an authorized source workspace. Returns a pending proposal for the user to confirm; does not create it. Unavailable for workspaces that workspace_status reports with remote_platform "windows".

tools.name: propose_tab_create
tools.description: Propose creating a terminal tab in an authorized workspace. Returns a pending proposal for the user to confirm; does not create it. Read workspace_status after confirmation to discover the new pane before proposing an agent start.

tools.name: propose_pane_split
tools.description: Propose splitting an existing pane in an authorized workspace, creating a new terminal pane to its right or below it. Use pane identifiers from workspace_status. Returns a pending proposal for the user to confirm; does not split it. Read workspace_status after confirmation to discover the new pane before proposing an agent start.

tools.name: propose_agent_start
tools.description: Propose starting an available agent in a pane of an authorized workspace. Returns a pending proposal for the user to confirm; does not start it.

tools.name: propose_agent_prompt
tools.description: Propose sending a prompt to an agent pane in an authorized workspace. Returns a pending proposal for the user to confirm; does not send it.

tools.name: propose_workspace_close
tools.description: Propose closing an authorized workspace and terminating its current panes and processes. Unsaved terminal work may be lost. Uses normal workspace close, never closes linked workspaces as a group, removes a Git worktree, deletes files, or deletes saved agent history. Returns a proposal handled by the current approval mode.

tools.name: propose_pane_close
tools.description: Propose closing an exact pane in an authorized workspace and terminating its processes. Closing the last pane also closes its tab/workspace; unsaved terminal work may be lost. Does not remove a Git worktree or delete saved agent history. Individual closes in multi-pane worktree-root workspaces are unavailable because Herdr cannot guarantee no group closure. Use identifiers from workspace_status. Returns a proposal handled by the current approval mode.

tools.name: propose_agent_close
tools.description: Propose closing an exact running agent by closing its pane and terminating its processes, as in the normal Close Agent Pane action. This is not prompt interruption or saved-history deletion. The last pane also closes its tab/workspace; unsaved terminal work may be lost. Does not remove worktree files. Individual closes in multi-pane worktree-root workspaces are unavailable because Herdr cannot guarantee no group closure. Use identifiers from workspace_status. Returns a proposal handled by the current approval mode.

tools.name: list_ranger_tasks
tools.description: List scheduled Ranger tasks in this turn's authorized scope and the current time and timezone. Use the current time before interpreting relative dates.

tools.name: propose_ranger_task
tools.description: Propose a Ranger task with an exact prompt, authorized workspace scope and schedule. Selected workspace and Agent reference identities within that scope are preserved for monitoring. A once schedule uses a future UTC ISO 8601 timestamp ending in Z. A daily schedule uses HH:mm and an IANA timezone; skipped DST times do not run and repeated times run once. An interval starts the given number of minutes after confirmation. Choose notification_mode agent for monitoring and follow-up requests: Ranger can notify only on meaningful requested outcomes or needed input, with its own title and body. The default status mode sends fixed run status notifications. Returns a pending preview: the task is enabled only when the user clicks Confirm. Scheduled tasks may read and propose operations; they never automatically confirm management actions. Ask the user if their schedule or timezone is ambiguous. Set all_workspaces when the user wants the task to cover every workspace, including ones created later: each run then uses every workspace Ranger may use at that time. scope is still required: give the workspaces to cover now; each run replaces it with those it covers.

tools.name: propose_ranger_task_update
tools.description: Propose edits to a scheduled Ranger task from list_ranger_tasks. Supply only fields to change. Preserves its workspace scope, model and bound Agent identities; changing those settings is unavailable through this tool. Never increases its approval mode; manual confirmation requires future workspace actions to be confirmed. Editing a paused task does not resume it. Returns a pending preview: the operation is applied only when the user clicks Confirm.

tools.name: propose_ranger_task_pause
tools.description: Pause future scheduled dispatch of a Ranger task while allowing its already-started run to finish. Use task_id from list_ranger_tasks. Returns a pending preview: the operation is applied only when the user clicks Confirm.

tools.name: propose_ranger_task_resume
tools.description: Resume a paused Ranger task. Cancelled tasks cannot resume. Use task_id from list_ranger_tasks. Returns a pending preview: the operation is applied only when the user clicks Confirm.

tools.name: propose_ranger_task_cancel
tools.description: Cancel a Ranger task permanently, stopping its active run and all future scheduled dispatch. Keeps its history. Use task_id from list_ranger_tasks. Returns a pending preview: the operation is applied only when the user clicks Confirm.

tools.name: propose_ranger_task_delete
tools.description: Delete an already cancelled Ranger task and its private run history. The task must have no remaining active or draining run. This cannot be undone. Use task_id from list_ranger_tasks. Returns a pending preview: the operation is applied only when the user clicks Confirm.

tools.name: send_user_notification
tools.description: Request a notification for a meaningful outcome or needed user input covered by this confirmed task. Use completed for verified success and attention for failure or required user input. event_key must identify the same Agent session and observed outcome across runs; reuse the exact key for an unchanged event and consult prior notification receipts. Use a concise title and body grounded in fresh workspace evidence, without credentials or authorization URLs. The server chooses the recipient and task link. A receipt records acceptance or deduplication, never proof of device delivery. Stay quiet while the monitored state is unchanged or non-actionable.
